properties.value: Available spare. The drive's own threshold is usually 5 to 10%.

panels.title: Wear used
panels.description: Share of rated endurance used. A line that climbs faster than before points at a new heavy writer. Lines mark 80% (watch) and 95% (replace).

targets.expr: label_match(max by (machine,drive,model,serial) ((label_replace(label_replace(last_over_time(nvme_smart_percentage_used[15m]),"machine","$1","host","(.*)"),"drive","$1","device","(.*)") or label_replace(label_replace((last_over_time(truenas_smart_wear_used_percent[15m]) or last_over_time(truenas_smart_nvme_percentage_used[15m])) * on(disk,serial) group_left(model) last_over_time(truenas_disk_info[15m]),"machine","truenas","",""),"drive","$1","disk","(.*)"))), "machine", "$machine")

panels.title: Spare capacity
panels.description: Available spare capacity of NVMe drives. It only falls once a drive starts retiring worn out cells.

panels.title: Temperature
panels.description: Lines mark 50 C and 70 C. The etcd stalls showed the pve NVMe 18 C hotter during each stall.

panels.title: Data written
panels.description: Total data written over the life of each NVMe drive (NVMe data units of 512,000 bytes). The slope is the write load.

panels.title: Media errors
panels.description: Media and data integrity errors logged by NVMe drives. Cumulative: any rise means new damage.

panels.title: Pending and reallocated sectors
panels.description: Sectors a hard disk or SATA SSD could not read (pending) and sectors it has remapped (reallocated). A count that keeps growing means the disk is failing.

panels.title: Root filesystem used
panels.description: Root filesystem of the machines running node_exporter: k8s-main and the two Pi-holes. k8s-main and the Pi-holes live on the pve NVMe drive, so these also say how full its thin pool is getting. pve itself has no node_exporter.

panels.title: ZFS pool used
panels.description: Allocated share of each TrueNAS pool, as `zpool list` counts it. TrueNASPoolUsageHigh alerts at 80%.

panels.title: pve NVMe reports
panels.description: Seconds since the pve host last pushed its NVMe SMART log (every 5 minutes). PVENVMeHealthMetricsMissing fires after 25 minutes.

panels.title: TrueNAS reports
panels.description: Seconds since the TrueNAS health cron job last pushed (every minute). TrueNASHealthMetricsMissing fires after 15 minutes.

panels.title: Drives that cannot be read
panels.description: Drives whose SMART log could not be read on the last run. They are missing from the table until they answer again.

panels.title: Machines with node_exporter
panels.description: k8s-main and the two Pi-holes. Their drives are not readable from inside an LXC guest, only their filesystem use.

options.content:
**Not covered yet**

- **Gaming PC SATA drives and hard disks.** Only its NVMe drives are read (smartctl, every 5 minutes, see `apps/gaming-pc`). A SATA drive has no standard wear or spare field. The PC reports only while it is on, so its rows go empty 15 minutes after it shuts down.
- **Proxmox Backup Server datastore.** `pbs_datastore_available` says whether it mounts, not how full or worn it is.
- **Pi-hole, tailscale and k8s-main drives.** They are LXC guests on the pve NVMe drive and have no disk of their own: their wear is the pve drive's. Only their root filesystem use is shown.
- **pve filesystem use.** The host has no node_exporter, so thin pool and root usage are not reported.
- **UPS.** NUT runs on the TrueNAS host and pve is a client, but no battery charge, load or runtime is collected. The netdata `nut_ups` plugin on TrueNAS only reports its own run time.
- **Hard disk temperature and age before the next TrueNAS deploy.** They appear once the updated health cron job has run on the NAS.

title: Hardware health
